newsitem.title: USA: Gull restated 1995 earnings for unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Gull restated 1995 earnings for unit sale.

text.p: Gull Laboratories Inc said Wednesday that it has restated its 1995 financial statements related to the sale that year of a portion of its European operations.
The restatement is required as part of its planned acquisition of the diagnostic business of the Intensive Care and Diagnostic Division of Fresenius AG, it said.

Gull Chief Executive and President George Evanega said in a statement that in January 1995 the company sold the operations and intangible assets relating to its German operations to Fresenius, a 55-percent shareholder, for about $313,500 of cash proceeds.
Gull recognized a gain on the transaction of $140,437 equal to the minority interest percentage. The remaining $173,063 was recognized as a contribution to capital by Fresenius.

However, in response to comments by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the 1995 financial statements have been restated to show the entire $313,500 as a contribution to capital, reducing other income and net income by $140,437.
The restatement decreased 1995 earnings per common and common equivalent share by $0.02 to $0.03. The company said the restatement would not affect the ongoing operations and earnings for 1997.
Gull develops, manufactures and markets diagnostic test kits for the detection of infectious diseases, cardiovascular diseases and autoimmune disorders.
